nonop.text: Interest Expense. Interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 decreased $0.7 million compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to a lower principal balance of debt outstanding during the third quarter of 2026 . Refer to Note 11 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for further details.

tax.text: Income Taxes. Our effective income tax rate decreased to 24.2% in the third quarter of 2026, from 25.9% in the third quarter of 2025 as a result of changes from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the “OBBBA”) that became effective in the third quarter of 2025.

net.text: Net Income. Net income was $145.4 million, or $4.34 per share of common stock on a diluted basis, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $82.2 million, or $2.45 per share of common stock on a diluted basis, for the third quarter of 2025. Results for the third quarter of 2026 included an after-tax benefit of $31.6 million, or $0.94 per share of common stock, for tariff refunds partially offset by after-tax charges of $0.2 million, or $0.00 per share of common stock , for restructuring. Results for the third quarter of 2025 included after-tax charges of $1.5 million, or $0.05 per share of common stock , for restructuring.

ocf.text: We generated $278.9 million of net cash provided by operating activities in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $247.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The increase in net cash provided by operating activities was primarily related to higher net income, including the favorable impact from tariff refunds received, which was partly offset by elevated working capital levels and the benefit in the prior year of lower income tax payments from the OBBBA. Working capital increases were due to higher accounts receivable attributable to higher net sales and higher inventory due to inflation and strategic inventory investments to support data center demand.

da.text: The net increase in net sales due to foreign exchange was mostly due to the favorable impact of the depreciation of the U.S. dollar against the Australian dollar and Chinese yuan partially offset by the appreciation of the U.S. dollar against the euro in the third quarter of 2026. We cannot predict whether foreign currencies will appreciate or depreciate against the U.S. dollar in future periods or whether future foreign exchange rate fluctuations will have a positive or negative impact on our net sales.

wc.text: Free cash flow increased in the first nine months of 2026 when compared to the first nine months of 2025, primarily due to higher net income, including the favorable impact from tariff refunds, which was partly offset by higher working capital levels, increased capital expenditures, and the benefit in the prior year from lower cash tax payments. Working capital increases were due to higher accounts receivable attributable to higher net sales, and higher inventory due to inflation and strategic inventory investments to support data center demand.

capex.text: We have no off-balance sheet arrangements that have, or are reasonably likely to have, a current or future effect on our financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources that is material to investors .

fcf.text: Free cash flow is a non-GAAP measure that does not represent cash provided by operating activities in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Therefore, it should not be considered an alternative to net cash provided by or used in operating activities as an indication of our performance. The cash conversion rate of free cash flow to net income is also a measure of our performance in cash flow generation. We believe free cash flow and cash flow conversion rate to be an appropriate supplemental measure of our operating performance because it provides investors with a measure of our ability to generate cash, repay debt, pay dividends, repurchase stock and fund acquisitions.

intro.text: In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, references to “the Company,” “Watts Water,” “Watts,” “we,” “us” or “our” refer to Watts Water Technologies, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Watts Regulator Co. was founded by Joseph E. Watts in 1874 in Lawrence, Massachusetts. Watts Regulator Co. started as a small machine shop supplying parts to the New England textile mills of the 19th century. Since then, Watts has grown into a global manufacturer and become one of the world’s leading providers of water technologies and solutions that are designed to promote safety, energy efficiency, and water conservation for commercial and residential buildings. Watts Water Technologies, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware in 1985 and is the parent company of Watts Regulator Co.

nonop.text: Interest Expense. Interest expense increased $6.5 million, or 79.3%, in 2024 as compared to 2023 primarily due to a higher principal balance of debt outstanding due to the acquisition of Bradley in the fourth quarter of 2023 and an increase in interest rates. Refer to Note 12 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further details.

tax.text: We are subject to income taxes in the U.S. (federal and state) and foreign jurisdictions. Significant judgment is required in evaluating our uncertain tax positions and determining our provision for income taxes.

net.text: Net Income. Net income for 2024 was $291.2 million, or $8.69 per common share on a diluted basis, compared to $262.1 million, or $7.82 per common share on a diluted basis, for 2023. Results for 2024 included after-tax charges of $10.7 million, or $0.32 per common share, for acquisition-related costs and $5.4 million, or $0.16 per common share, for restructuring, partially offset by after-tax benefits of $5.8 million, or $0.17 per common share, for a gain on the settlement of the Bradley pension plan, $3.5 million, or $0.11 per common share, for a gain on sale of assets and $1.0 million, or $0.03 per common share, for other investment gains.

ocf.text: We generated $361.1 million of net cash from operating activities in 2024 as compared to $310.8 million in 2023. The increase in cash generated was primarily due to higher net income, improved working capital and cash flows generated from acquisitions.

da.text: The organic decrease in SG&A expenses was primarily due to $10.3 million from productivity initiatives, a net decrease in short-term and long-term compensation accruals of $6.7 million, $3.3 million of restructuring saving, and decreases of $4.0 million in professional fees, $2.9 million in engineering project spend, $2.0 million in donations, $1.4 million in depreciation and amortization, $1.1 million in travel and marketing spend, and $1.1 million in insurance and product liability claim costs. These decreases were partially offset by general inflation of $16.7 million and an increase in investments of $16.3 million, including in our smart and connected initiatives and other strategic initiatives, compared to 2023. The decrease in foreign exchange was primarily driven by the appreciation of the U.S. dollar against the Canadian dollar and Chinese yuan, partially offset by the depreciation of the U.S. dollar against the euro. The acquired increase in SG&A related to the Bradley and Josam acquisitions in the Americas segment completed in the fourth quarter of 2023 and first quarter of 2024, respectively, as well as the Enware acquisition in the APMEA segment completed in the second quarter of 2023. The decrease in special items SG&A costs was primarily due to a $7.8 million gain on the settlement of Bradley’s frozen pension plan and $4.4 million gain on sale of buildings.

wc.text: Working capital (defined as current assets less current liabilities) as of December 31, 2024 was $665.6 million compared to $655.2 million as of December 31, 2023. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities was 2.6 to 1 as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023. The increase in working capital is primarily related to the increase in cash and cash equivalents as a result of increased cash from operating activities.

metrics.formula: (Net income − operating cash flow) / average assets; not annualized

metrics.label: Return on average assets
metrics.formula: Net income / average assets; not annualized

metrics.label: Current ratio
metrics.formula: Current assets / current liabilities

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

labels.d_oassets: Change in prepaid and other assets
labels.rou_add: Lease assets obtained for lease liabilities

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: In 2025, 2024 and 2023, no customer accounted for more than 10% of our total net sales.

Our top ten customers accounted for $570.3 million, or 23.4%, of our total net sales in 2025; $512.0 million, or 22.7%, of our total net sales in 2024; and $440.4 million, or 21.4%, of our total net sales in 2023.
In 2025, our top ten customers accounted for approximately 23% of our total net sales with no one customer accounting for more than 10% of our total net sales.
In 2025, 2024 and 2023, no customer accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s total sales or accounts receivable.
You should not rely on forward-looking statements because they involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.

Everything we accomplish depends on creating an environment that is engaging and supportive and enables employees to perform to their potential.

Our success depends on our ability to recruit, retain and develop highly-skilled management and key personnel.

While we presently intend to continue to pay comparable quarterly cash dividends on both Class A and B common stock, the payment of future cash dividends depends upon our Board of Directors’ assessment of our earnings, financial condition, capital requirements and other factors.
